chapter: Swing, singers, Ed Fox and recordings
title: Who arranged Rosetta, Angry and Japanese Sandman

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That same year you made another recording of "Rosetta"
Uh-huh.
Which, according to the story is originally arranged by Henri --
Henry Woods.
Henry Woods. And according to the story, it was rearranged by Cecil Irwin?
Uh-huh.
And then modified by you? Is that
It was?
That's what they say. If you modified it, what did you do?
What is it, "Rosetta"?
"Rosetta".
I don't know what I could have done to it.
Okay, so that's probably one of --
That must have been after Cecil left.
No, that was '34.
Still in the band.
I don't know what the heck kind of change I could have made on a Cecil Irwin arrangement. Unless I jazzed it up or something.
I don't know. Stanley Dance wrote that in the notes to the album.
Yeah?
And said that was the story. Didn't say it was true.
Didn't say it was true, said that was the story? You see, a lot of things you do, you don't think about it at the time. You don't know that it's going to go down in the history, or nothing.
Right. You know, I think when I do these interviews, if I were being interviewed, could I remember what I was doing when I was 16 years old, or 19 years old, something like that. That's tough.
Yeah.
You file those things away. There's also some question about who arranged "Angry" and "Japanese Sandman." Did you arrange those, or did Cecil arrange those?
I think Cecil arranged those.
Some people have given you credit for those two arrangements.
No, I don't remember it. I don't think I made "Angry." I think Cecil Irwin -- as I look at the copy of the arrangement on the stand, look at the handwriting on the title, it's Cecil handwriting.
